title: No Room in the Inn? What Luke Actually Says (Luke 2:7)
text: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn. The gospel never mentions an innkeeper. The Greek word often translated inn, kataluma, can also mean a guest room. Luke uses the same word later, for the upstairs room where Jesus shared the Passover meal. So perhaps the guest room was already full of relatives, and the baby was laid where the animals were fed. Either way, he was born at the edge of things.
